criterion: which type of entity the encyclopedia article describes

categories.name: Company
categories.definition: An organization engaged in commercial, industrial, or professional activities.

categories.name: Biological Taxonomy
categories.definition: A classification of living organisms, including species, genera, families, and orders.

categories.name: Ship
categories.definition: A large watercraft that travels the world's oceans and other sufficiently deep waterways.

categories.name: University
categories.definition: An institution of higher education and research, which grants academic degrees.

categories.name: Geographical Feature
categories.definition: A natural or artificial feature of the Earth's surface, such as a mountain, lake, or river.

categories.name: Book
categories.definition: A written or printed work consisting of pages glued or sewn together along one side and bound in covers.

categories.name: Album
categories.definition: A collection of audio recordings issued as a single item on CD, record, or another medium.

categories.name: Village
categories.definition: A small community or group of houses in a rural area, larger than a hamlet but smaller than a town.

categories.name: Person
categories.definition: An individual human being.

categories.name: Film
categories.definition: A motion picture or movie, a series of still images that create the illusion of moving images.

categories.name: Plant
categories.definition: A living organism of the kind exemplified by trees, shrubs, herbs, grasses, ferns, and mosses.

categories.name: Animal
categories.definition: A living organism that feeds on organic matter, typically having specialized sense organs and nervous system.

categories.name: Building
categories.definition: A structure with a roof and walls, such as a house, school, or factory.

categories.name: Historical Event
categories.definition: An occurrence or happening of significance in history.

categories.name: Journal
categories.definition: A periodical publication with scholarly articles on a particular academic discipline.

categories.name: Government
categories.definition: The governing body of a nation, state, or community.

categories.name: Crater
categories.definition: A bowl-shaped geological formation at the top of a volcano or created by the impact of a meteorite.

categories.name: Mountain
categories.definition: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level.

categories.name: River
categories.definition: A large natural stream of water flowing in a channel to the sea, a lake, or another river.

categories.name: Lake
categories.definition: A large body of water surrounded by land.

categories.name: Moth
categories.definition: An insect related to the butterfly, typically having a stout body and feathery or hairlike antennae.

categories.name: Spider
categories.definition: An eight-legged predatory arachnid with an unsegmented body consisting of a fused head and thorax and a rounded abdomen.

categories.name: Bird
categories.definition: A warm-blooded egg-laying vertebrate animal distinguished by the possession of feathers, wings, and a beak.

categories.name: Insect
categories.definition: A small arthropod animal that has six legs and generally one or two pairs of wings.

categories.name: Reptile
categories.definition: A cold-blooded, egg-laying vertebrate of a class that includes snakes, lizards, crocodiles, turtles, and tortoises.

categories.name: Fungus
categories.definition: A spore-producing organism feeding on organic matter, including molds, yeast, mushrooms, and toadstools.

categories.name: Fish
categories.definition: A limbless cold-blooded vertebrate animal with gills and fins living wholly in water.

categories.name: Mammal
categories.definition: A warm-blooded vertebrate animal of a class that is distinguished by the possession of hair or fur, secretion of milk by females for the nourishment of the young, and (typically) the birth of live young.

categories.name: Amphibian
categories.definition: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal of a class that comprises the frogs, toads, newts, and salamanders.

categories.name: Mollusk
categories.definition: An invertebrate of a large phylum that includes snails, slugs, mussels, and octopuses.

categories.name: Arachnid
categories.definition: An arthropod of the class Arachnida, such as a spider or scorpion.

categories.name: Bacterium
categories.definition: A member of a large group of unicellular microorganisms that have cell walls but lack organelles and an organized nucleus, including some that can cause disease.

categories.name: Virus
categories.definition: A small infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of an organism.

categories.name: Fictional Character
categories.definition: A person or being that exists in a fictional narrative or story.

categories.name: Mythological Figure
categories.definition: A character from a myth, a traditional story that explains a natural or social phenomenon.

categories.name: Legendary Figure
categories.definition: A character from a legend, a traditional story sometimes popularly regarded as historical but unauthenticated.

categories.name: Folklore Figure
categories.definition: A character from folklore, the traditional beliefs, customs, and stories of a community, passed through the generations by word of mouth.

categories.name: Deity
categories.definition: A god or goddess in a polytheistic religion.

categories.name: Supernatural Being
categories.definition: A being that exists beyond the observable universe and is not subject to the laws of nature.

categories.name: Alien
categories.definition: A being from another world or planet.

categories.name: Robot
categories.definition: A machine capable of carrying out a complex series of actions automatically, especially one programmable by a computer.

categories.name: Artificial Intelligence
categories.definition: A branch of computer science dealing with the simulation of intelligent behavior in computers.

categories.name: Computer Program
categories.definition: A collection of instructions that performs a specific task when executed by a computer.

categories.name: Software
categories.definition: The programs and other operating information used by a computer.

categories.name: Hardware
categories.definition: The machines, wiring, and other physical components of a computer or other electronic system.

categories.name: Gadget
categories.definition: A small mechanical or electronic device or tool, especially an ingenious or novel one.

categories.name: Tool
categories.definition: A device or implement, especially one held in the hand, used to carry out a particular function.

categories.name: Instrument
categories.definition: A tool or implement, especially one for delicate or scientific work.

categories.name: Machine
categories.definition: An apparatus using mechanical power and having several parts, each with a definite function and together performing a particular task.

categories.name: Vehicle
categories.definition: A thing used for transporting people or goods, especially on land, such as a car, truck, or cart.

categories.name: Aircraft
categories.definition: A vehicle that is able to fly by gaining support from the air, or in general, the atmosphere of a planet.

categories.name: Spacecraft
categories.definition: A vehicle or device designed for travel or operation in outer space.

categories.name: Satellite
categories.definition: An artificial body placed in orbit around the earth or moon or another planet in order to collect information or for communication.

categories.name: Rocket
categories.definition: A cylindrical projectile that can be propelled to a great height or distance by the combustion of its contents, used typically as a firework or signal.

categories.name: Missile
categories.definition: An object that is forcibly propelled at a target, either by hand or from a mechanical weapon.

categories.name: Weapon
categories.definition: A thing designed or used for inflicting bodily harm or physical damage.

categories.name: Explosive
categories.definition: A substance or device that can cause an explosion.

categories.name: Chemical
categories.definition: A compound or substance that has been purified or prepared, especially artificially.

categories.name: Element
categories.definition: A substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

categories.name: Mineral
categories.definition: A solid inorganic substance of natural occurrence.

categories.name: Gemstone
categories.definition: A precious or semi-precious stone, especially one cut, polished, and used in a piece of jewelry.

categories.name: Metal
categories.definition: A solid material that is typically hard, shiny, malleable, fusible, and ductile, with good electrical and thermal conductivity.

categories.name: Alloy
categories.definition: A metal made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

categories.name: Compound
categories.definition: A thing that is composed of two or more separate elements; a mixture.

categories.name: Mixture
categories.definition: A substance made by mixing other substances together.

categories.name: Solution
categories.definition: A liquid mixture in which the minor component (the solute) is uniformly distributed within the major component (the solvent).

categories.name: Suspension
categories.definition: A mixture in which particles are dispersed throughout the bulk of a fluid.

categories.name: Colloid
categories.definition: A homogeneous non-crystalline substance consisting of large molecules or ultramicroscopic particles of one substance dispersed through a second substance.

categories.name: Emulsion
categories.definition: A fine dispersion of minute droplets of one liquid in another in which it is not soluble or miscible.

categories.name: Gel
categories.definition: A semi-solid colloidal suspension of a solid dispersed in a liquid.

categories.name: Foam
categories.definition: A mass of small bubbles formed on or in liquid, typically by agitation or fermentation.

categories.name: Paste
categories.definition: A thick, soft, moist substance typically produced by mixing dry ingredients with a liquid.

categories.name: Powder
categories.definition: A dry, bulk solid composed of a large number of very fine particles that may flow freely when shaken or tilted.

categories.name: Granule
categories.definition: A small compact particle of a substance.

categories.name: Crystal
categories.definition: A piece of a homogeneous solid substance having a natural geometrically regular form with symmetrically arranged plane faces.

categories.name: Fiber
categories.definition: A thread or filament from which a vegetable tissue, mineral substance, or textile is formed.

categories.name: Textile
categories.definition: A type of cloth or woven fabric.

categories.name: Fabric
categories.definition: Cloth produced by weaving or knitting textile fibers.

categories.name: Material
categories.definition: The matter from which a thing is or can be made.

categories.name: Substance
categories.definition: A particular kind of matter with uniform properties.

categories.name: Matter
categories.definition: Physical substance in general, as distinct from mind and spirit; (in physics) that which occupies space and possesses rest mass, especially as distinct from energy.

categories.name: Energy
categories.definition: The strength and vitality required for sustained physical or mental activity.

categories.name: Force
categories.definition: Strength or energy as an attribute of physical action or movement.

categories.name: Power
categories.definition: The ability or capacity to do something or act in a particular way.

categories.name: Authority
categories.definition: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience.

categories.name: Control
categories.definition: The power to influence or direct people's behavior or the course of events.

categories.name: Influence
categories.definition: The capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something, or the effect itself.

categories.name: Impact
categories.definition: The action of one object coming forcibly into contact with another.

categories.name: Effect
categories.definition: A change that is a result or consequence of an action or other cause.

categories.name: Result
categories.definition: A consequence, effect, or outcome of something.

categories.name: Outcome
categories.definition: The way a thing turns out; a consequence.

categories.name: Consequence
categories.definition: A result or effect of an action or condition.

categories.name: Repercussion
categories.definition: An unintended consequence occurring some time after an event or action, especially an unwelcome one.

categories.name: Ramification
categories.definition: A consequence of an action or event, especially when complex or unwelcome.

categories.name: Implication
categories.definition: The conclusion that can be drawn from something, although it is not explicitly stated.

categories.name: Inference
categories.definition: A conclusion reached on the basis of evidence and reasoning.

categories.name: Conclusion
categories.definition: The end or finish of an event or process.

categories.name: End
categories.definition: A final part of something, especially a period of time, an activity, or a story.

categories.name: Finish
categories.definition: Bring (a task or activity) to an end; complete.

categories.name: Completion
categories.definition: The action or process of finishing something.
